rationale: The two feedback capacitors control receiver frequency response and each has a known modeled 120-kohm shunt, rather than sharing a supply-decoupling bank. They are accessible in one original photo. Three frequencies distinguish obvious network-dominated readings from a useful capacitance estimate without removing parts.
interpretation: These are fitted-board network readings, not automatically individual capacitor values. C21 is modeled across R24 (120 kohm); C22 across R26 (120 kohm). Cp helps separate a parallel resistive contribution. The 0.1-V level reduces semiconductor excitation but does not isolate the IC. Frequency dependence and loss will guide whether a useful estimate is supported. A stable reading alone cannot exclude other parallel capacitance, prove a nominal tolerance or certify receiver operation.
analysis_rules: Retain raw capacitance model, units, D, frequency, voltage and instability reports.
If Cs rather than Cp is reported with D, derive Cp = Cs / (1 + D**2), retaining the original Cs.

For a simple parallel equivalent with positive Cp and D, G = 2*pi*f*Cp*D and Rp = 1/G. Compare with the modeled 120-kohm shunt, allowing other board paths; a large D is not automatically a bad capacitor.
Frequency consistency is a screening test only. Do not mark the individual value measured or lower the unknown-value count unless alternate network contributions are independently bounded.
No results or component values are prefilled.

next_batches.action: Select C18/C23/C25 only after this first batch shows whether the method is useful; no all-capacitor sweep yet.
C5 lead pitch and LED pad geometry can be measured without repeating the known body sizes; select exact dimensions only if accessible while fitted.
RF, PIR, receiver enable and motor/control timing remain queued for the user-deferred scope session; no repeated DC or diode sweep.

excluded_now: C5/C6 share supply nodes, so a fitted measurement would not recover each independently.
Tuning capacitors interact with antenna and switching devices; no direct individual-value claim from a two-terminal sweep.
D6 breakdown testing through PIC is not requested.
Previously completed Q1, Q7, diode and antenna checks are not repeated.
